doc.title: Don Wolff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996

title: Sound quality on old films
summary: Rowe marvels at the balance of old recordings and Wolff comments on equipment.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: I’m quite impressed usually by the balance of the sound. The sound itself is dated, but you can hear everything, which sometimes really amazes me. Like what technology did they have back then, did they just hang a microphone and they let the band balance themselves perhaps?

Well some of our greatest treasures come from people using little microphones and recording at concerts. But that particular session was well recorded. I never have any problems with the sound, but it depends on what kind of equipment you have to show it on and yesterday we had some wonderful equipment so you got to hear the sound that I hear at home, which is not often the case when I’m showing these kinds of films. Because if you don’t have good sound equipment, you don’t get the kind of sound you heard yesterday.
